This affects the rendering pipeline, and is a feature that could multiply performance of any game that isn't reaction-time-focused. this will help the newer users of Godot make an enjoyable game instead of dropping development and quitting altogether when they hit optimisation bottlenecks and realize how much it takes to optimize. The ratio of assets that aren't optimized for gaming, to all the easily-available assets is high too, forcing many to take a longer route in dissapointment. Optimisations are still crucial, but this will smoothen out the learning curve and make game development more acessible. Not everyone can code DOOM.

Frame batching essentially multiplies frame rate and provides a great peformance boost where no optimisation can be achieved, at a cost that doesn't always matter.
